title: Strategic model trajectory scan and ops triggers
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Goal: Produce a compact, operationalized runbook and dataset that helps product and ops teams detect shifting model supply/quality velocity and translate that signal into concrete routing/rollback/autoscale triggers for Redwood deployments.

Background: The model landscape changes rapidly (new weights, quantization releases, vendor availability fluctuations). Sales and SRE teams repeatedly ask for a way to translate market signals into operational decisions: when to prefer a different model family, when to enable aggressive quantization, or when to move traffic to Dedicated. Existing signal artifacts are ad hoc — this ticket builds an integrated ‘trajectory scan’ that combines model capability velocity (feature releases, latency/cost regressions) with supply risk (availability, license churn) to produce ops triggers and a prioritized backlog for PM/Eng.

Scope & deliverables:
- A scored model-trajectory dataset (CSV + sampling harness) that captures weekly signals for ~40 candidate models across pricing, latency, quantization readiness, and vendor stability.
- A small scenario simulator (not heavy infra) that runs 4 supply-shock and 4 feature-velocity scenarios and outputs recommended operational actions (e.g., failover to model X, enable prefix caching, escalate to Dedicated).
- A decision runbook with 6 ops triggers (thresholds and escalation steps) that can be translated into the Console’s rollout automation and alerting rules.
- A one-page executive brief and a 2-hour cross-functional workshop to validate assumptions with Eng, SRE, and Solutions.

Approach:
1) Data sources: consolidate signals from internal benchmarks (latency/cost runs), third-party model release feeds, GitHub/weights manifest scraping, and partner availability pings.
2) Feature engineering: compute velocity metrics (weekly delta in latency, token-cost, pass-rate on core evals) and risk metrics (downtime events, license changes, regional capacity constraints).
3) Scoring: combine into a normalized trajectory score (0-100) and a directional tag (improving/regressing/volatile).
4) Simulation: craft several synthetic demand shapes (low-throughput interactive, high-throughput batch, short-context RAG) and apply supply-shock events to produce recommended operational actions.
5) Runbook: codify thresholds and human-in-the-loop escalation steps; map triggers to Console automation knobs (route policy, fallback model mapping, quantization profiles).

Constraints & assumptions:
- This is an MVP: the simulator will be a lightweight notebook + scripts, not production orchestration.
- We will prioritize models currently in the Redwood catalog (~40) and expand later.
- External signal freshness: we assume at least weekly refresh for public signals.

Risks:
- Signal noise leading to false positives. Mitigation: conservative thresholds and manual review gate.
- API/benchmarks coverage gaps across regions. Mitigation: mark gaps as data-quality and defer automated triggers until coverage improves.

Success metrics:
- Completed dataset and simulation delivered by due_date.
- At least 3 ops-trigger mappings accepted by SRE/Console PM.
- Workshop attendance: representatives from Eng, SRE, Solutions, and 2 enterprise account reps.

- Week 4: cross-functional workshop and finalize deliverables.
